Action: Consider identity and access management for your service (ORR 16)
What it means: Enable users to securely access the digital services and information they need while protecting departmental data and systems.
Why does this exist:
- provide a consistent and secure user experience in your service or product
- reduce the number of identities and passwords users need to manage
- improve security through modern authentication and authorisation controls
- enable services to adopt common departmental identity standards and platforms
- reduce duplication of effort and technology across services
Conditions: If a service requires users to securely access the service or information
What needs to happen:
When exploring (disco and alpha) user journeys, think about whether you will need users to log-in or create an account (authentication).

If so, consider in what capacity users will be interacting with your product or service (as a citizen, on behalf of an organisation, on behalf of the DfE, or a combination)
 
When building (beta), engage with Dominic Harley if you are unsure which is the right option for your service and users. Or, if you know what solution fits your service best, engage directly with the onboarding team
Standards applicable: Identity Management B2B,Identity Management B2C,Identity Management B2E
Systems:
- GOV.UK One Login
- DfE sign-in
- Entra ID - Single Sign-on
